A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same COMBO paper, with 24 readable pages including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered pages 2–24 are identical; first-page differences are confined to affiliations and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments and ablations in Section 6, additional analyses in Appendix C, and human–robot experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results, including the benchmark evaluations and five real-world human–robot trials.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 and Algorithm 1 are identical, retaining the compositional video diffusion model, agent-dependent loss scaling, world-state estimation, VLM submodules, and tree-search planning.

E1.justification: Both evaluate TDW-Game, TDW-Cook, adapted 2D-FetchQ, and the real-world human–robot puzzle task. Cooperator policies and agent-count scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–3, 5, and 7, including the planning baselines, BC-single/BC-GAIL/Co-GAIL, AVDC, and the simpler supervised submodule model.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, observations, training settings, and sample counts are unchanged. Both retain the 20-episode main TDW evaluation, 60-episode 2D-FetchQ replay evaluation, and five real-world trials.

E4.justification: The Intent Tracker and loss-scaling ablations, search-budget and agent-count studies, alternative-submodule comparison, and Appendix C prediction and failure-case analyses are identical.

E5.justification: Both use the same point estimates and episode/trial aggregation. Seed information, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, and significance tests are absent from both.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match. Examples include COMBO's 81.3% success rate in Table 2 and the 4/5 successful real-world trials with 8.4 average successful-trial steps in Table 8.

T1.justification: The DEC-POMDP formulation, diffusion definitions, compositional reasoning, and Equations 1–8 are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain identical claims about compositional world modeling, cooperative planning, and generalization across tasks, cooperators, and agent counts.

C2.justification: The explanations of cooperation performance, intent adaptation, VLM advantages, and generation failures are unchanged, as are the limitations concerning inference speed, diverse cooperators, and hidden physical variables.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B and C.2 retain identical architecture, data collection, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time details. Resource links and their destinations are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and comparisons with prior research are identical. The affiliation edits do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: On page 1, Zheyuan Zhang's affiliation changes from the University of Michigan to the University of Massachusetts Amherst; remaining affiliation numbers are adjusted and Massachusetts Institute of Technology becomes MIT. The arXiv stamp is updated. Scientific prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened first-page affiliation block no longer extends beyond the main text's right margin. Figures 1–13, Tables 1–8, their captions, and all layouts on pages 2–24 remain identical.

improvement.justification: v3 updates affiliations and the version stamp, with a small improvement in first-page text fit. The scientific content, empirical evidence, analyses, reproducibility information, and appendices are identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality change.
